info.title: Common local API
info.description: OpenAI-compatible inference endpoints under /v1 plus Common extensions under /api. Binds 127.0.0.1 by default. Every error body has the OpenAI shape with a stable Common `code` (see Error). When the server was started with an API key, every route except /health requires `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Browser requests (an `Origin` header) are accepted only from the allow-listed desktop origins; any other origin, a cross-site fetch, or (without an API key) a non-loopback `Host` gets 403 `policy_denied` before the route runs.

tags.name: mesh
tags.description: Common Mesh (M3): peer networking, pairing, trust, privacy and audit. Everything is off by default; nothing leaves this device unless privacy is `trusted_group` and the request names a paired device with `target`.

get.description: Always 200 while the process runs. Never requires authentication.

200 when a request could be served now: no model is loaded (the server can accept a load), or the loaded engine answers a tokenize round-trip within 2 s. 503 while a load holds the slot or the engine is unresponsive.

Text exposition format. Metrics: common_requests_total{route,status}, common_requests_rejected_total{reason}, common_tokens_generated_total, common_prompt_tokens_total, common_ttft_seconds (histogram), common_decode_tokens_per_second, common_queue_depth, common_inflight. Never contains prompt or completion text.
Every model in the local store plus catalog entries not downloaded yet. Each object carries a `common` extension with download/load state.

post.description: Loads `model` on demand (single slot). Models whose GGUF has a chat template get the template applied by the engine; models without one (e.g. the stories15M fixture) are prompted with plain `role: content` lines. `response_format` of type json_schema/json_object enables constrained decoding. With `stream: true` the response is text/event-stream: OpenAI chat chunks, a final chunk with finish_reason, a usage chunk when stream_options.include_usage is set, then `data: [DONE]`. Closing the connection cancels generation.
Raw prompt (string or single-element array), no chat template. Same sampling, streaming and admission rules as chat.
Loads `model` in embeddings mode (reloading the slot if it was loaded for generation).

get.description: Fresh `common_hardware::probe()` report: cpu, memory, gpus, backends, disk.

Never waits on a model load (the slot is read without blocking). `engine.state` is `loading` while a load runs (`loading_model_id`, `loading_for_ms`), else `ready` with a model loaded, else `idle`. `loaded` is the loaded model as of the last moment no load or request held the slot.
Store manifests plus catalog entries not downloaded, each with a memory estimate and a fit verdict for this device (GGUF-based when the blob is present, file-size-only otherwise).

post.description: text/event-stream of progress objects; the last one has `done: true`. A failure is sent as an Error object and ends the stream. Re-running resumes a partial download.

429.description: Two downloads are already in progress

post.summary: Load a model into the single slot

post.description: The path SIGTERM takes, for callers that cannot signal the process (the desktop app on Windows): in-flight generations are cancelled, HTTP connections get up to 5 s to drain, the peer endpoint is closed (mDNS goodbye, QUIC close) and the loaded model is unloaded (engine stopped), then the process exits. No body. Same auth, origin and Host checks as every route.

delete.description: Unloads it first if loaded; deletes the manifest and the blob when no other manifest shares it.

post.description: Hashes and links the file into the store; the file is not moved. `path` must be absolute.

put.summary: Switch peer networking and serving on or off
put.description: Persisted in `COMMON_HOME/config.json` (0600). `enabled` binds (or closes) the authenticated QUIC endpoint, mDNS advertising/browsing and the inbound accept loop; `serve_peers` lets paired devices in a group whose policy allows it run models here. A change restarts the endpoint, so open peer connections are re-established; devices disconnected by you (`POST /api/peers/{id}/disconnect`) stay disconnected unless networking is turned off. When the endpoint cannot start, networking is recorded as off and the error is returned. The same file's optional `peer_quota` object (`requests_per_minute`, `tokens_per_minute`, `max_concurrent`; defaults 120, 200000, 4; 0 = unlimited for the two rates) limits what each paired device may run here and is read when the daemon starts: a peer request beyond it, or one that finds no free engine slot (the daemon's `--max-concurrent` slots), gets `overloaded` at the sending device; a peer never waits in the local queue, and peer generations across all devices are capped at `max_concurrent` and at one fewer than the engine slots, so a peer never holds the slot local work needs (`peer_slots` in the status; 0 with `--max-concurrent 1`, which serves no peers).

get.description: `peers` are pinned devices with `connected`, `health`, `last_error` and their groups. `discovered` are devices mDNS currently sees, never this device; `trusted` is true only when pinned here and never a trust decision by itself (the transport's verifier decides). `unreachable` are devices mDNS sees with a valid signed record but at no address this device can dial (only IPv6 addresses: the peer endpoint is IPv4 only); they are never dialled from discovery. `revocations` are the signed revocations this store holds.

delete.description: Removes the pin and closes its connections. The device may pair again (use revoke to forbid that).

post.description: Unpins it, records a revocation signed by this device, closes every connection to it with the REVOKED close code and sends the revocation to the connected devices that shared a group with it here, which apply it too and pass it on the same way; every new connection offers it again until that device has sent it back, and a device that already holds it ignores it. The revoked key fails inside the TLS handshake from now on; audit `peer_revoked`.

post.summary: Connect to a paired device now, optionally at a given address
post.description: For networks that drop mDNS and devices whose IP changed. Nothing is sent for an id that is not paired here (403 `peer_unauthorized`). Dials `addr` (when given), then the addresses mDNS sees, then the pinned `last_addr`; an open connection is returned as is. Every address is only a hint: the TLS handshake must present the device's pinned key, so another device at that address is refused (403 `peer_unauthorized`) and nothing is stored. A refusal closed before the device proved its pinned key with control data (a TLS alert such as `certificate_revoked`, an early close) cannot be told from one forged on the path, so it reads the same (403 `peer_unauthorized`, "did not prove it is …") and the next address is tried; so does a close before the device's Hello that claims a protocol mismatch (with the hint "if it is that device, update Common on both devices") or a frame-size close. `last_addr` changes only after a handshake at that address returned the connection. Clears the device's redial backoff. 403 `policy_denied` while networking is off; 403 `peer_revoked` when this device revoked it (or the device closed with that code after proving its key); 403 `peer_held` when the device disconnected this one (it said so on the control stream; either ends the dial); 426 `protocol_incompatible` only when proven (the device's Hello was read with another major, or this device's own negotiation failed); 502 `peer_lost` when nothing answered; 504 `timeout` for a control handshake that did not finish.

addr.description: ip:port where the device can be reached now (not port 0, an unspecified or a multicast address).

post.summary: Open a pairing window and show the code
post.description: Requires peer networking on. One window at a time (409 `overloaded` while one is open). Opens the separate accept-any pairing endpoint for `expires_at - now` seconds, advertises `pair=1` on mDNS and returns the single-use 6-digit code, `pair_addr` (the `ip:port` another device dials; the LAN address of the default route when the endpoint is bound on every interface) and the QR payload carrying that address (`common-pair:v1:<peer id>:<ip:port>:<secret>`). More than 5 wrong codes lock the window (`pairing_locked`); turning networking off closes it (`cancelled`). `GET /api/pair/status` reports the outcome.

name.description: This device's name as the other side will see it (<= 64 bytes); empty or absent: this host's name (`device_name` in GET /api/network).

pair_addr.description: ip:port of the pairing endpoint as another device dials it

get.summary: Outcome of the current or last pairing window

post.description: Connects from this device's peer endpoint (networking must be on) to `addr` (the other device's pairing endpoint `ip:port`, required with a 6-digit code) and runs the SPAKE2 exchange bound to the TLS session. `code` may instead be the whole QR payload, whose address and expected peer id are then used: any other device that answers fails the TLS handshake (`pairing_failed`, audit reason `qr_peer_mismatch`) and nothing is pinned on either side. On success both devices pin each other; a wrong code is `pairing_failed` (401), a locked window `pairing_locked` (429).

name.description: This device's name as the other side will see it; empty or absent: this host's name.

put.description: A paired device can run or serve a workload only through a group whose policy allows that kind; the default policy denies everything. Returns the full list.

get.summary: Privacy mode and the disclosure text

put.description: `local_only` (default) always succeeds. `trusted_group` requires `"acknowledged": true`; without it the response is 403 `policy_denied` whose message is the disclosure text the user must see (a paired device decrypts and reads the prompt it runs). `swarm_allowed` is refused until its security gate. Persisted; audited as `privacy_changed`.

get.description: The last `n` events (1..=1000, default 100) of `COMMON_HOME/logs/audit.jsonl`, oldest first: pairing, connections, revocations, settings changes and remote requests. Ids, counts, codes and durations only; never prompt text or key material. A request sent to a peer leaves `remote_request` entries on both devices: on the sender `phase: sent` before anything leaves (the request is refused when it cannot be written) then `phase: finished` (outcome, `request_id`), on the server one entry with the outcome and the same `request_id`.

Every chat, completion and embeddings request this daemon runs or sends to a paired device, and every request it serves for one (`kind: served_for_peer`), from the moment its handler starts (before admission, so a request waiting for a slot shows as `queued`, and one to a paired device as `connecting` until it is sent) until it ends; then the last 256 finished, newest first. In memory only: cleared when the service restarts. Ids, counts, codes and durations only, never prompt or completion text.

post.summary: Disconnect a paired device until you connect it again
post.description: Closes every connection to the device with the `CLOSE_HELD` close code (audit `peer_disconnected`, reason `by_user`) and holds it: this device dials it no more (its own requests to it get 403 `policy_denied`) and refuses its connections (audit `peer_rejected`, reason `held`, once per hold); the device reads `peer_held`. `POST /api/peers/{id}/connect` ends the hold, and so does turning networking off and on or restarting the service; another settings change (Sharing) keeps it. Revocations still cross the hold: each time the device dials this one, the two exchange the revocations due at the other before this device closes the connection (both on protocol minor 1 or later), so a revocation made on either side reaches the other at the device's next redial. The device stays paired. 403 `peer_unauthorized` for a device not paired here; 403 `policy_denied` while networking is off.

PeerId.name: id
PeerId.description: A device's 64-hex peer id, or the `xxxx-xxxx-xxxx` short label of a paired device.

Target.name: X-Common-Target
Target.description: Same as the body field `target`; the body wins when both are present.

ClientRef.name: X-Common-Client-Ref
ClientRef.description: The caller's own id for this request, shown as the job's `client_ref` in `GET /api/jobs`; any other value is ignored, and so is a ref a job still listed already holds (a ref names one request). Allowed in CORS preflights.

Error.description: Error in the OpenAI shape with a stable Common code

context_note.description: Set when the planner changed what was asked for: context capped to the trained context, reduced to fit memory, or the KV cache downgraded.

target.description: Common extension. `local` runs here. `peer:<peer id or short label>` runs the whole request on that paired device (remote execution; the device decrypts and reads the prompt). Allowed only when privacy is `trusted_group`, networking is on and the device is pinned, not revoked and in a group allowing remote inference; otherwise 403 `policy_denied` / `peer_unauthorized` / `peer_revoked` before anything runs or connects. Every response echoes `target`.

listen_addr.description: `ip:port` of the QUIC endpoint while enabled.

peer_id.description: This device's 64-hex id (its Ed25519 public key).

device_name.description: This host's name (the Computer Name on macOS, the hostname on other unix, COMPUTERNAME on Windows): the default name a paired device sees.

dial_addr.description: `ip:port` other devices should dial (the default-route address when the endpoint is bound on every interface); null while networking is off or when no route gives one.

peer_slots.description: Peer generations this device runs at once across all devices: `peer_quota.max_concurrent`, at most the engine slots (`--max-concurrent`) minus one.

PeerQuota.description: `config.json` `peer_quota` in force (read at daemon start): per paired device, requests per minute and generated tokens per minute (0 = unlimited; a request's whole max_tokens is charged when it starts) and generations at once (also the cap across all devices, see `peer_slots`).

health.description: Liveness from keep-alives (F-02-05), updated within one keep-alive interval: `unhealthy` = still open but 3 intervals without a datagram; `reconnecting` = lost, a reconnect is expected; `disconnected` = closed on purpose, networking off, or never connected since networking started.

last_error.description: The latest failed dial to this device since its last connection (either direction); null when there is none or networking is off.

held.description: Disconnected by this device's user (`POST /api/peers/{id}/disconnect`) until Connect, turning networking off and on, or a service restart (a Sharing change keeps it); false while networking is off.

connection.description: The connection in use; null while not connected.

PeerCapabilities.description: What the device signed and sent when this connection opened (verified against its pinned key, not independently checked), re-typed here; never its raw JSON. `hardware` and `free_memory_bytes` were measured when the device's networking started, not at `issued_at_utc`.

protocol_minor.description: The minor version this connection negotiated.

issued_at_utc.description: When the record was signed: at this connection's handshake.

hardware.description: null when the device's report does not parse as this version's HardwareReport.

id.description: This device's store or catalog id for that file; null when it knows no such file.

PeerConnectionInfo.description: The live connection to a device. Byte counts are UDP payload bytes since it opened, keep-alives included; `id` is new for every connection, so rates are taken between two readings with the same id.

last_exit.description: The last engine that exited on its own (killed, crashed) since the daemon started; its slot was freed and the next request starts it again. Null when none has.

reason.description: As the OS reported it, e.g. `signal: 9 (SIGKILL)` or `exit status: 1`.

in_flight.description: Streams and calls the exit cut off (each ended with `backend_failed`).
Streams and calls using the model.

loaded_for.description: `local`, or `peer:<hex>` when a paired device's request loaded it.

Job.description: One request. Every key is always present; null means not known (yet). Durations in ms are measured on this device: `queue_ms` from arrival to admission (to the request leaving, for one sent to a device), `load_ms` the model step after admission (near 0 when the model was loaded), `ttft_ms` from arrival to the first streamed piece, `duration_ms` arrival to end. `prompt_ms`, `decode_ms` and `decode_tokens_per_second` are the engine's (for a request sent to a device, that device's engine).

id.description: The response id (`chatcmpl-…`, `cmpl-…`); `embd-…` for embeddings; the requesting device's `request_id` for `served_for_peer`.

state.description: `queued` waiting for an engine slot, `connecting` a request to a paired device (no slot or load here) while this device reaches it, through the dial until the request is sent on the connection, `loading` in the model step, `running` generating (or sent to the device); `cancelled` when the requester went away or stopped it (`error_code` `cancelled` or `client_gone`). Daemons before `connecting` report that phase as `queued` with a `peer:` target; a client should read an unknown state as not known, never as an outcome.

completion_tokens.description: Counted per streamed piece while active; the engine's count once done.

finish_reason.description: From a paired device, at most 32 characters.

request_id.description: Requests to or from a paired device; the `request_id` of both devices' `remote_request` audit entries.

device_actual.description: Where the local engine runs it, e.g. `Metal0 (Apple M2)`; null for a request sent to a device (not reported).

reason.description: `link_local_only`: heard only at IPv6 link-local addresses; `other_family`: heard only at IPv6 addresses, some routable.

addrs.description: IPv4 ip:port addresses from the signed record, best first (routable before loopback and link-local, lowest first).

code.description: An Error code, e.g. peer_lost (nothing answered), peer_unauthorized (another device or key at that address, or it refused this one).
